hook.line: Open an old novel, a legal letter or a newspaper editorial and you will meet *hubiese* and *fuese*. They look like new verbs. They are not: they are a twin of a form you already know, and spotting the twin is enough.
hook.es: Si lo hubiese sabido, no habría venido.
hook.en: If I had known, I wouldn't have come.

examples.es: Si lo hubiese sabido, no habría venido.
examples.en: If I had known, I wouldn't have come.
She asked me to be punctual.

examples.es: Si tuviese más tiempo, viajaría más.
examples.en: If I had more time, I would travel more.
They wanted us to eat with them.

examples.es: Me dijo que hablase más despacio.
examples.en: He told me to speak more slowly.

examples.es: Si Rosa lo hubiese sabido, no lo habría vendido.
examples.en: If Rosa had known, she wouldn't have sold it.

examples.es: Si lo hubiera sabido, no habría venido.
examples.en: If I had known, I wouldn't have come.

rule:
You already know the past subjunctive ending in *-ra*: *hubiera*, *fuera*, *tuviera*. It has a twin ending in *-se*, with exactly the same meaning and uses:
*hubiese*, *fuese*, *tuviese*, *hablase*, *comiese*

So *Si lo hubiese sabido* and *Si lo hubiera sabido* are the same sentence.

The endings are *-se, -ses, -se, -semos, -seis, -sen*, and *nosotros* gets an accent: *hubiésemos*, *comiésemos*.

In Colombia you will see the *-se* form mostly in books, news and formal letters, so recognise it and keep saying the *-ra* form yourself.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the imperfect subjunctive in *-se*. The *-ra* and *-se* forms are two spellings of one tense.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *hubiese* or *habría* and type the whole sentence: *Si lo ___ sabido, no habría venido.*
yourTurn.answer: Si lo hubiese sabido, no habría venido.
accept: Si lo hubiera sabido, no habría venido.
yourTurn.why: The *if* half takes *hubiese* (or *hubiera*); *habría* belongs to the result half.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *fuese* or *fue* and type the whole sentence: *Me pidió que ___ puntual.* (She asked me to be punctual.)
yourTurn.why: After *pidió que*, the past subjunctive *fuese* (or *fuera*) is needed, not the simple past *fue*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it using the *-se* form: If I had more time, I would travel more.
yourTurn.answer: Si tuviese más tiempo, viajaría más.
accept: Si tuviera más tiempo, viajaría más.
yourTurn.why: *Tuviese* is *tuviera* with the *-se* ending, and the result half uses *viajaría*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it using the *-se* form: They wanted us to eat with them.
yourTurn.why: *Comiésemos* is the *nosotros* form, with the accent on the vowel before *-semos*.

yourTurn.prompt: Rewrite it with the *-ra* twin: *Si lo hubiese sabido, no habría venido.*
yourTurn.answer: Si lo hubiera sabido, no habría venido.
yourTurn.why: Swap *-se* for *-ra* and the meaning stays the same.

yourTurn.prompt: Rewrite it with the *-se* twin: *Si hubieran vendido el café, Tomás se habría ido.*
yourTurn.answer: Si hubiesen vendido el café, Tomás se habría ido.
yourTurn.why: *Hubieran* and *hubiesen* are the same form in two spellings.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about Rosa: *Si lo hubiese sabido, no habría venido.*
yourTurn.answer: Si Rosa lo hubiese sabido, no habría venido.
accept: Si lo hubiese sabido Rosa, no habría venido.
yourTurn.why: The form *hubiese* is the same for *yo* and *ella*, so the name does the work.

pitfalls.wrong: Si lo habría sabido, no habría venido.
pitfalls.right: Si lo hubiese sabido, no habría venido.

pitfalls.wrong: Si lo hubiese sabía, no habría venido.
pitfalls.right: Si lo hubiese sabido, no habría venido.
pitfalls.why: After *hubiese* comes the participle *sabido*, not the past form *sabía*.

pitfalls.wrong: Si hubiesemos salido antes, no habríamos perdido el tren.
pitfalls.right: Si hubiésemos salido antes, no habríamos perdido el tren.
pitfalls.why: The *nosotros* form of this tense always carries an accent on the vowel before *-semos*.

personal: Say one thing you wish you had done differently, starting with *Ojalá* or *Si*. For example, *Ojalá lo hubiese sabido.*
